title: What is a derivative?
intro: A short explainer video with two questions along the way.
transfer: Look at a curve from your everyday life (e.g. temperature over the day) and estimate where it is steepest.

scenes.caption: A curve and two points on it. The straight line through both is called a secant. Its slope: the difference in height divided by the distance.
Now the second point moves closer and closer to the first. The secant turns with it.
In the limit, the line touches the curve at only one point: the tangent. Its slope is the derivative at that point.
If you zoom in far enough, the curve there looks almost like a straight line, with exactly this slope.

questions.prompt: What happens to the secant when the second point moves closer?
options: It becomes steeper at every point
It disappears completely from the picture
It moves closer to the tangent
questions.explanation: As the point moves closer, the secant approaches the tangent.

questions.prompt: What does the derivative at a point tell you?
options: The slope of the tangent there
The highest point of the curve
questions.explanation: The derivative is the slope of the tangent at that point.
